turns.thought:
Yes, definitely — Airplane Mode being ON is exactly why you have no signal bars. It switches off all of your phone's wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), so no amount of rebooting will bring service back while it's on.

**To turn it off:**
- **iPhone:** Open **Control Center** (swipe down from the top-right corner — or up from the bottom on older models) and tap the **✈️ airplane icon** so it's no longer highlighted. Once it's off, you should see signal bars and a network indicator (5G/LTE) appear within a few seconds.
- **Android:** Swipe **down from the top of the screen** twice to open the Quick Settings panel, then tap the **Airplane mode** tile to turn it off.

If your status bar continues to show Airplane Mode after you've tried toggling it, try toggling it **off and on and then off again**, or reboot once more with it already off.

Notably, Airplane Mode was likely the underlying issue here all along, separate from the billing suspension — the suspension was real (line 555-123-2002 was suspended as of today), and that's now resolved, but Airplane Mode would have kept you offline regardless.

Give that a try and let me know what your status bar shows afterward — I can help troubleshoot further if you're still not getting signal.
